what_happened: The person running Athena reviewed the drain log and records at the 13 Nov 11:42 UTC update. They saw that the idea "refuse a reading that skips or drops a part of the request" had been built or tried five times across three lines since 10 Nov, for about $37. The five tries were the acceptance-point check (twice, paused), the skipped-acceptance-point line (twice, paused), and the drop-a-named-part line today ($7.76), where planning never converged. Nothing had recorded that these were one recurring idea, and nothing had asked whether it was worth building. No job is named in the event, and it lists no unmet criteria or failed checks. The person running Athena reported the pattern and changed nothing by hand.
cause: Athena tracks work per job and per line. It has no record that groups requests by the idea they pursue, and no running total of spend per idea. Each request therefore looks new, and a worth-building check never fires. The stop-after-three and stop-and-diagnose rules count repeated rejections of one topic, but they are paused. Nothing replaced them, so nothing signals "this idea keeps failing" across lines.
other_causes: Each line was worded differently (acceptance-point, skipped-acceptance-point, drop-a-named-part), so even a text match on topic would not group them.
Pauses and planning non-convergence end a line without a diagnosis, so no finding says why the idea keeps failing.
The error review and planner have no step that asks whether a recurring fix is worth its cost.
open_hypotheses: Whether the five tries failed for one shared reason or for different reasons. The event does not say.
Whether the idea is worth building at all. The event gives cost but not how often readings actually drop a part of a request.
Whether the paused stop-after-three rule would have caught this chain if it were active.
contradictions: The event says the five tries came from 3 lines. Stop rules that count per topic could in principle have grouped them, but they are paused, so nothing in the input shows whether they would have fired.
prevention: Give each request an idea tag, set when it is queued from a failure review, a steward item or an earlier job. Athena would keep a per-idea record of tries, outcomes and total spend. When an idea reaches three tries or a spend threshold, it would stop queuing more tries on it. It would then ask the owner or steward a single question: build it differently, drop it, or keep going. The answer would be recorded as a decision. That would have stopped the chain at three tries, before the $7.76 fifth, and put the worth-building question in front of the right person.
proposed_request: Add a per-idea tracker for repeated tries. Outcome: when a request or follow-up is queued, Athena links it to the earlier requests that pursue the same idea. Use explicit links first, such as the cited job, the failure-review source and the steward item. Use a title match only as a hint. Athena keeps the count of tries, the outcomes and the total spend for each idea. When an idea reaches 3 tries, or its spend passes a cap set in athena.toml, Athena holds further queued tries on that idea. It then puts one question on the decisions page: is the idea worth building, and if so what should change. A recorded decision releases or closes the held items. Acceptance: (1) given the recorded history of the five 'refuse a reading that drops a part of the request' tries since 10 Nov, the tracker groups them as one idea and shows 5 tries and about $37; (2) a test replays that history and shows the third try is held and a decision question appears; (3) a request on an unrelated topic is not held; (4) athena status shows held ideas with their try count and spend; (5) the CHANGELOG.md entry is added.
